deepdive.divline: No dividend change mentioned; focus on deleveraging post-capex peak

profile.entities: Borosil Limited (Parent); Stylenest India Limited (Subsidiary); Borosil Scientific (Related Party Manufacturer)
profile.subseg: Borosilicate Glassware; Opalware (Larah); Non-Glassware (Hydra Flasks, Appliances)
profile.themes: China Dumping Pressure; BIS Quality Control Orders; Gas Cost Inflation; Import Substitution (Hydra)

bull_bear.body: Funding via mix of internal accruals (INR 119 Cr operating cash flow FY26), debt, and equity. Net debt rose to INR 49.7 Cr due to working capital (inventory build for QCO). No dividend change mentioned; focus on deleveraging post-capex peak.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Continued Chinese dumping in borosilicate glass delaying anti-dumping relief; Delay in BIS certification for appliances; Gas price volatility; Inventory obsolescence if demand remains muted; Execution risk on new Hydra lines.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic long-term, acknowledging short-term headwinds. Transparent about China dumping impact and gas cost pressures. Confident in structural growth (Make in India) once supply chain normalizes.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Borosil is the ONLY manufacturer of borosilicate glass in India; competitors source from China. The 'cost advantage' of local mfg is currently negated by Chinese dumping and higher Indian gas costs, making anti-dumping duty critical. Related party mfg with Borosil Scientific (cost+5%) prevents asset duplication but limits full margin capture until insourced.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Glassware: INR 295.5 Cr (+17.3% YoY), 66% own mfg; Opalware (Larah): INR 411.9 Cr (+7.3% YoY), 90-95% utilization; Non-Glassware: INR 463.7 Cr (+2.4% YoY), severely impacted by Hydra BIS QCO shortages (est. INR 100 Cr lost sales).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gas costs up 2.5x, Chinese dumping pressures margins | Borosil Limited | loser | High | Directly impacted by INR 30-35 Cr annualized gas inflation and inability to pass on costs immediately due to cheap Chinese imports. |
| BIS QCO blocked imports, creating supply gap | Borosil Limited | beneficiary | High | Once in-house Hydra production starts (Q1/Q2 FY27), BL captures full manufacturing margin vs previous trading model, estimated 10% gross margin uplift. |
| Chinese glass dumpers face potential anti-dumping duties | Unlisted Chinese Exporters | loser | Med | Anti-dumping investigation ongoing (6-9 months timeline); if imposed, levels playing field for BL's borosilicate glass. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin compressed to 11.5% (vs 14.2% YoY) due to West Asia gas crisis (gas costs up 2.5x to ~INR 50 Cr/yr impact) and Chinese dumping. Price hikes of 8-10% implemented but with 1-2 quarter lag in pass-through. Solar plant to offset ~INR 28 Cr cost.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth target 15-20% YoY; Medium-term EBITDA margin target ~20%; FY27 Capex guidance INR 110 Cr (INR 90 Cr growth + INR 20-25 Cr maintenance); Solar plant (20MW) commissioning Q1 FY27 expected to save INR 28 Cr EBITDA annually.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - B2C inventory-driven model. Management notes high inventory levels in appliances (due to QCO pre-buying) and glassware (production > sales due to furnace efficiency constraints), expecting inventory drawdown in FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: In-house Hydra manufacturing (3 lines) starting Q1/Q2 FY27 to capture trading margins (~10% gross margin expansion); Bharuch glassware facility (jars/jugs) by Q3 FY27 (INR 42 Cr); Furnace debottlenecking (25T to 32T) planned FY27/28 (INR 50 Cr).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 was a consolidation year with flat EBITDA due to Hydra supply chain disruptions (BIS QCO) and 2.5x gas cost inflation from West Asia crisis, masking underlying volume growth in glassware. The thesis hinges on the commissioning of in-house Hydra manufacturing in Q1/Q2 FY27 to recover ~10% gross margin and the potential imposition of anti-dumping duties on Chinese borosilicate glass to stabilize pricing power.
